messages:
From: Sana Malik <sana@clearwell.health>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC environment & MAP — prerequisites and timeline

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the demo last week. ClearWell is excited to run a 4-week evaluation with Redwood. Before we lock dates, the procurement and infra teams need a clear mutual action plan that spells out the environment setup items we must complete to get the POC live. The key items are: API keys, org/tenant setup, IP allowlist, and VPC peering.

Can you share a short MAP (one-pager) that lists the steps, owners, and target dates? We’re aiming to start infra provisioning the week of June 7 and have a gating checklist in place by June 14.

Also, who on your side will own the VPC peering coordination with our network team? We’ll likely need a minimal set of CIDR ranges and a peering template to hand to our cloud ops team.

Sana Malik
Director, IT Engineering
ClearWell Health

Sana —

Great to hear — excited to run this with ClearWell. I’ve put a draft MAP together and attached it (MAP-draft-ClearWell.pdf) along with a lightweight network requirements sheet that your cloud ops can use (network-reqs.xlsx). High-level plan (short):

- Week of Jun 7: Org & tenant creation + API key provisioning (ClearWell network team provides CIDR/IPs) — owner: ClearWell + Redwood onboarding lead
- By Jun 10: IP allowlist applied and health check of control-plane connectivity — owner: ClearWell infra / Redwood support
- Jun 11–13: VPC peering handshake and routing validation using peering-template.yaml — owner: Redwood solutions eng (Marissa) + ClearWell cloud ops
- Jun 14: Gate review and sign-off; start POC traffic Jun 15

Marissa (cc’d) will run the peering and keys playbook with your cloud ops. If the dates above work we’ll bake them into the MAP and include a short escalation path in case we hit firewall/peering issues. I’ll also add the HubSpot deal id to the MAP so procurement has a single reference.

Next steps: 1) confirm the CIDR ranges you’ll use; 2) confirm who from your network team I should meet with (name + email); 3) we’ll schedule a 30-min gating call Thursday 5/29 to walk the MAP.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP-draft-ClearWell.pdf (application/pdf), network-reqs.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: POC environment & MAP — prerequisites and timeline

Hi Sana / Jordan —

Quick technical runbook to make the POC handoff as frictionless as possible. I’ve included the minimal commands and the peering template we use internally — attaching peering-template.yaml.

1) Organization and tenant setup
   - We need a customer tenant org created in our control plane for ClearWell. Please provide the primary org name and an admin contact (email).
   - We will provision two API key scopes: "admin-provision" (for initial platform setup) and "runtime" (for POC service calls). Admin keys expire after 30d; runtime keys are long-lived but can be rotated.

2) API key provisioning (Redwood steps)
   - Once org is created, reply here with the admin contact.
   - We will generate the admin-provision key and send it in a secure link (DocuSign/credentials vault) to your admin.
   - Example curl to validate runtime key after provisioning:
     curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <RUNTIME_KEY>" https://api.redwood.com/v1/health

3) IP allowlist (customer action)
   - Provide the egress IPs/CIDRs that will originate evaluation traffic and any on-prem NAT IPs that must be permitted.
   - On our side, we’ll add your CIDRs to the control-plane allowlist within 24 hours of receipt and confirm by email.

4) VPC peering (joint action)
   - Required items from ClearWell: VPC ID, primary CIDR, region, and the contact for your cloud network engineer.
   - We provide: peering-template.yaml (attached) and route table guidance.
   - Typical handoff sequence: create peering request (ClearWell), accept (Redwood), update route tables (both sides), run connectivity tests (Redwood infra will run tokenized probe).

5) Gate criteria for Jun 14 sign-off
   - Admin and runtime keys provisioned and validated
   - Control-plane connectivity successful (API health checks pass)
   - IP allowlist in place and pings/traceroutes show expected paths
   - VPC peering accepted and routes propagated

If helpful I can run a 30–45 minute technical workshop with your cloud ops on Tue 6/8 (PST) to walk through the peering steps.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
---
Attachments: peering-template.yaml (text/yaml)

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the workshop.

—
Sana Malik
Director, IT Engineering
ClearWell Health
